claim: For waiting fees, CW-F06's window runs to boarding instead of 'the same window as CW-F04' that FX1 requires. The builder's justification does not hold for waiting fees. Routine late-arrival messages after the free wait therefore become STRONG again, which brings back FX1's false escalation for CW-WAITING (in scope).
action: fixed: CW-F06's window for a waiting fee now ends where CW-F04's window ends (free wait, or boarding if earlier); no-show keeps arrival to cancellation

claim: The phrase-list stand-in for CW-F06's new reading step is tuned to the verbatim E01, E03 and E07 strings and misreads common nearby wording. A lateness admission ('I'm waiting for the lift') becomes PLACES/STRONG and is escalated, which is the exact error FX1 removes. Placing or contesting wording ('where r u', 'here already') becomes UNCLEAR and gets an approval-tier uphold instead of escalation.
action: fixed: message reader rewritten (presence questions, Singapore English place words, apostrophe variants, wait requests no longer LATE, LATE needs no place word); 78 message readings checked by the build

claim: CW-F06's new definition starts 'during the wait' at the arrival indication for every source, rider GPS included, but the engine still counts rider GPS only from the wait anchor. For a Ryde advance booking where the driver arrives early, the rule card and the reference engine therefore give different outcomes.
action: fixed: rider GPS counted from the arrival indication, like calls and messages (variant V67)

claim: The new self-tests copy the E01, E03 and E07 wording but not their timing or fee type. The E01 and E07 messages were sent after the threshold (free wait), and E07 is a waiting fee. So the post-threshold window segment for the LATE patterns, and the whole waiting-fee window, are untested.
action: fixed for no-show: V68 (late message after the threshold); waiting fees have no engine path, recorded as open item D31

claim: FX2 wording and labeling details: FC-R03's name still says 'metered'; the credibility_note's source date is wrong for the main source; the playbook leaves out one new source and the driver's response.
action: fixed: FC-R03 renamed; the exclusion moved to new rule FC-R00 with the RydeTAXI articles as sources; playbook lists 900004230226 and the driver's response

claim: For waiting fees, CW-F06's window runs to boarding. Any rider GPS ping at the pin, or any message such as 'I'm here' or 'where are you?' sent after the free wait and before boarding, therefore becomes STRONG counter-evidence. That contradicts Ryde's waiting-fee condition and CW-R05 (A), departs from FX1's required window, and the credibility_note's justification is false for waiting fees. This brings the FX1 defect back for CW-WAITING.
action: fixed (same as A1-FID-1)

claim: FC-R03 keeps credibility C, but its new METERED exclusion carries Ryde's CW-R00 scope condition over to detour refunds. Under the KB's own credibility_principle that makes it D, and it has no FAIRRYDE label. The credibility_note is wrong on two counts. The exclusion does decide the outcome (it alone turned E10's S$9.60 refund into ESCALATE_HUMAN). And the rule's own source note names as its 'basis' a non-RydeTAXI article that is older than 12 months (B) and is one side of a META-04 known conflict.
action: fixed: new eligibility rule FC-R00, credibility D, FAIRRYDE label for the inference; FC-R03 back to its v0.1 sources and credibility C

claim: FC-R03's stated reason goes beyond its sources and leaves out the grounds the sources do give. 'Leave taxi fares to the taxi company' stretches 'fees ... follow that of the respective taxi company' into a handling role that no Ryde text states. 'No basis for a refund computed by the platform' is equally true of RECALCULATED fares. The real distinguishing facts (cash-only fare collected by the driver, and the KB's own REFUND_DECIDER model) and ToU s.10/s.20 are not given to the reviewer.
action: fixed: FC-R00 states what the articles say (fees follow the taxi company, meter fare keyed in, cash only) and that Ryde publishes no refund rule

claim: For METERED fares, FC-R05 attaches a 'difference' computed with TAXI_TARIFF, which is one operator's tariff (ComfortDelGro, C). The cited RydeTAXI source says charges vary by taxi company, and the rule gives the reviewer no warning about this.
action: fixed: FC-R00 warns that TAXI_TARIFF is one operator's tariff

claim: CW-F06's source note and D27 say more than Jasper actually confirmed. He confirmed three case verdicts. He did not confirm the rule design, and in particular not the window to boarding, which departs from FX1. That choice is not recorded as an open decision.
action: fixed: CW-F06 source note says Jasper confirmed the three outcomes; the reading rule is FairRyde's design

claim: CW-F06 does not say how to treat a message that fits both readings. The engine treats such a message as UNCLEAR (reading test, then APPROVE), a rule the text does not contain. A reader of the text could instead rate it STRONG under the first clause.
action: fixed: CW-F06 says a message that fits neither reading or both is unclear

claim: The FC-R05 zh leaves out 'fee tiers and surcharges' from the recomputation basis. This gap predates A1 but sits in a rule A1 changed.
action: fixed: FC-R05 zh includes fee tiers and surcharges

claim: FC-R03's name still says 'metered', which contradicts the new statement that excludes METERED fares.
action: fixed: FC-R03 name says recalculated fare

claim: When a rider asks the driver whether they are coming or on the way, the engine reads it as the rider admitting lateness (LATE). These questions contest the driver's marked arrival, but no reading test runs on LATE, so the fee is upheld automatically. The exclusion for driver-directed 'coming' only covers the two exact forms 'you coming' and 'u coming'. 'on the way', 'omw' and 'almost/nearly there' have no exclusion at all.
action: fixed: questions about the driver ('uncle coming?', 'are you on the way?') read PLACES and are removed before the LATE check (variant V65)

claim: A rider who states their place in words outside the narrow PLACE list, and also asks the driver to wait, is read LATE, so the fee is upheld automatically. The LATE list contains polite wait requests ('pls wait', 'can wait', 'wait for me') that riders send from the pick-up. The PLACE list misses void deck, carpark, block or blk, 'reach' or 'reached', 'already there', and 'downstairs' or 'here' without 'I'm'. LATE wins whenever PLACES misses.
action: fixed: polite wait requests are no longer LATE cues; place words added; any place word blocks LATE

claim: The engine normalizes only the U+2019 apostrophe and needs 'i'?m' with no space. Other apostrophes common on phones and Chinese IMEs (U+2018, fullwidth U+FF07, backtick), 'I m' with a space and 'Iam' all miss every first-person PLACE pattern. Alone they read UNCLEAR, which is safe. With any LATE token they read LATE, giving AUTO.
action: fixed: apostrophe variants normalized; 'i m', 'im', 'iam' match

claim: The place-contest pattern needs 'wrong' before the noun, so a contest written the other way round ('the pin is wrong', 'my location is correct') is not PLACES. Combined with 'coming over' or 'pls wait', it reads LATE, giving AUTO.
action: fixed: 'the pin is wrong', 'my location is correct' read PLACES

claim: The acknowledgment list includes 'yes', 'yep', 'ya' and 'sure' and is read without the driver's preceding message. A 'yes' answering the driver's 'Are you at the lobby now?' places the rider, but it reads NEUTRAL. NEUTRAL contacts never get the reading test, so the fee is upheld automatically. The card only exempts an acknowledgment such as 'ok'.
action: fixed: 'yes', 'ya', 'sure' read UNCLEAR (variant V66)

claim: The rule card now defines one window for all rider-side evidence ('from the driver's arrival indication (the wait anchor when there is none) to the cancellation'). The engine counts rider messages from the arrival indication (t_arr) but rider GPS from the anchor. In an advance booking the anchor is the later scheduled time, so the same placement counts when it is a message and not when it is a tier A GPS record.
action: fixed (same as A1-FID-3)

claim: Safe-direction misreading, but frequent. Two common admissions are read PLACES and escalated to a person, which brings back FX1's over-escalation of routine cases. (a) 'I'm waiting for the lift' and 'I'm outside <somewhere else>, N min' read PLACES because 'I'm' + waiting/outside/here matches whatever follows. (b) A rider's own wrong-pin admission reads PLACES because 'wrong pin/entrance/location' matches whoever is at fault.
action: fixed: 'waiting for the lift' reads LATE; a rider's own wrong-pin or wrong-entrance admission reads UNCLEAR

claim: V58 is labeled as the E07 pattern (a waiting fee), but it runs the no-show playbook on V06. The engine cannot run a waiting-fee case at all, and A1's rerun covered only E01 to E04. So the new 'to boarding' window that FX1 asked for has no executable check.
action: partly: V58 relabeled; a waiting-fee path in the engine is open item D31

claim: For waiting fees, CW-F06's window now runs to boarding. That makes the routine message a late rider sends on reaching the car ('I'm downstairs', 'where are you?') STRONG counter-evidence, which brings back FX1's over-escalation for CW-WAITING (an in-scope ADJUDICATE type). The credibility_note's justification does not hold for waiting fees. The deviation from FX1's required 'same window as CW-F04' is not recorded in open_items: D27 is silent on it and D30 covers only the window start.
action: fixed (same as A1-FID-1); the window choice is recorded in CW-F06's credibility_note and D27

claim: The rider explanation still tells the rider 'no call or message from you in the trip record' whenever no rider contact falls inside the wait. That is false when the rider messaged before the arrival indication (the D30 case) or after the cancellation (new self-test V64).
action: fixed: explanation names rider calls or messages outside the wait instead of saying there were none (V64)

claim: PB-CW-WAITING was not updated for FX1. It has no CW-F06 step and does not require chat logs, yet step 8 checks CW-R12, which depends on F-RIDER-EVIDENCE from CW-F06. FX1's new waiting-fee definition therefore has no consumer in the waiting playbook, which the kb_applier route follows for E07. PB-FC-ROUTE was updated for FX2 in the same commit.
action: fixed: PB-CW-WAITING has a READ CW-F06 step and requires chat logs

claim: After FX2, the reason code FC-R-DETOUR-CONFIRMED and FC-R03's own name still say the rule covers metered fares with a PARTIAL_REFUND outcome. This contradicts FC-R03's new statement and invites the E10 failure again.
action: fixed: TX-REASON FC-R-DETOUR-CONFIRMED label says recalculated fare

claim: CW-F06 now defines one window for all STRONG items, starting at the driver's arrival indication. The engine applies it to rider calls and messages (from t_arr) but still checks rider GPS from the wait anchor, so the two kinds of evidence get different windows, and the engine disagrees with the rule for rider GPS. This is outcome-changing for a constructed case. I rate it MAJOR because the engine is a verification tool and no organizer or round 1 case carries rider GPS.
action: fixed (same as A1-FID-3)

claim: Several labels and notes still describe CW-F06 in the old terms ('rider-side system evidence' as the thing CW-F06 detects; reading only the statement). Under the new rule a rider message can exist and still not be counter-evidence.
action: fixed: NO_RIDER_EVIDENCE label and the ontology note on rider_called_driver

claim: The rider sentence for UNCLEAR contacts always uses the plural 'calls or messages', even for one item. It also states the contested reading as a fact of the record, although for V62 the rider's own message says 'I'm here' and the engine itself flags the reading as decisive.
action: fixed: separate sentences for calls and unclear messages, singular and plural, no claim about what was said

claim: D30 puts v0.2 behavior in the default_v0_1 field. The arrival-to-cancellation-or-boarding window was introduced in v0.2, so the field label is wrong for this entry.
